samples.summary: api-keys URL/method/body are never asserted after the fetch→requestUrl rewrite
samples.evidence: `apiKeysUrl()` (http-client.ts:383-397) is new code: it rebuilds the management URL (`${server}/workspaces/${encodeURIComponent(workspace)}/api-keys`), now percent-encodes workspace and key id, and moves GET/POST/DELETE + the `{name}` body into `requestUrl`. Every test that touches these calls stubs fetch with `vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(...)` (upstream-error.test.ts:219-228 and 376-383) which returns the same response for ANY url/init, and the only assertion on fetch args is `retryHeaders.Authorization` (line 409-411). Nothing asserts the request URL, the HTTP method, or the POST body — so if the rewrite had pointed api-keys at `this.base` (`/api/v1/workspaces/...`), dropped the DELETE method, or lost the `{name}` payload, every test here would still pass while all three commands broke in production. Searched the whole cli package for `api-keys|apiKeysUrl|listApiKeys|createApiKey|revokeApiKey` and for `toHaveBeenCalledWith(` in packages/cli/test; no test pins these request arguments.
searchedFor: read packages/cli/test/output.test.ts around the api-keys reference

Removing the `.slice(0, MAX_UPSTREAM_CODE)` would leave the suite green. Grepped packages/cli/test for `repeat(` and `MAX_UPSTREAM`; only message/stack cases exist.

finding.evidence: `apiKeysUrl()` (http-client.ts:383-397) is new code: it rebuilds the management URL (`${server}/workspaces/${encodeURIComponent(workspace)}/api-keys`), now percent-encodes workspace and key id, and moves GET/POST/DELETE + the `{name}` body into `requestUrl`. verdict.reason: Verified the gap myself. http-client.ts:383-398 builds the api-keys URL (management base, not `this.base`), percent-encodes workspace/id, and passes method + `{name}` body into requestUrl (177-194), which assembles method/headers/body. Every test touching those methods stubs fetch with a url/init-agnostic mock (upstream-error.test.ts:219-228, 376-383); the only request-arg assertion in the whole CLI test suite for these calls is `retryHeaders.Authorization` (409-411). I looked beyond the reviewer's searches: the dry-run request-shape assertions exist but only for sheets tabs (tabs.test.ts:91-101,146-156) and api-keys.ts has no --dry-run path (dry-run.ts:13 builds only /api/v1 URLs); docs-content.test.ts:301-337 is the only other real-client fetch test and asserts response body, not request; `DELETE` appears in no CLI test file; backend api-key-http.e2e-spec.ts builds its own paths so it cannot catch a wrong CLI URL. No counterexample exists — a rewrite pointing api-keys at /api/v1, dropping DELETE, or losing the {name} body would keep all tests green, so the changed request-construction behavior has no meaningful test.

finding.summary: `sheets cells batch` and `sheets import` were converted to `forwardUpstreamError` but no test drives either through a failing upstream response
finding.evidence: The delta changes `!res.ok` handling in packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts (batch, line ~146) and packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-import.ts (line ~90), yet the new CASES table in upstream-error.test.ts (lines 218-245) — introduced with the comment "Every other command that talks to the backend" — lists sheets cells get/set/delete but not `sheets cells batch`, and lists `sheets export` but not `sheets import`. Grep over packages/cli/test for `batchCells`/`sheets import` finds only output.test.ts:315 (malformed --data JSON, fetch never called) and schema/namespace tests, none of which exercise a non-ok response. These are the two paths with extra pre-request logic (stdin/CSV parsing, dry-run, imported-count merge), so a site that regressed to `throw new Error('HTTP <status>')` there would ship undetected — precisely what the end-to-end block claims to prevent.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the CASES table in packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts omits `sheets cells batch` and `sheets import`. Both are present: lines 287-290 register the argv ['sheets','cells','batch','doc-1','--data','{"A1":{"value":"1"}}'] and line 291 registers ['sheets','import','doc-1', importCsv] with a real temp CSV written at lines 252-253 so the file-read/CSV-parse pre-request logic actually executes. The loop at lines 305-322 expands every case into two tests that stub fetch with ok:false at status 404 (Express body) and 409 (documented envelope) via stubFetch (lines 219-228), then assert the exact stderr envelope and process.exitCode === 1. The runs go through the real commander program built by buildProgram() (lines 230-243), which registers registerSheetsCommand -> registerCellsCommand/registerSheetsImportCommand (sheets.ts:15-16), so control reaches the converted sites at cells.ts:147 and sheets-import.ts:91. Neither test is short-circuited: no --dry-run flag, valid --data JSON, and the CSV file exists. A comment at lines 284-286 explicitly names these two as the converted sites with the most room to stop reaching forwardUpstreamError. The reviewer's grep for 'batchCells|sheets import' missed them because the table stores argv fragments as separate string literals.
